prompt: Task.java is provided and complete. Finish TaskList.java so it stores Task objects in an ArrayList and can add them, mark one done by title, list the pending ones sorted by priority, and count the finished ones.
explanation: TaskList is a thin wrapper around an ArrayList<Task>: every method is a loop over that one field. markDone works because the list stores object REFERENCES, so calling setDone on the Task it found changes the object the list already holds. pending() builds a brand new ArrayList and sorts that copy, which is why callers cannot disturb the stored order, and List.sort is stable so equal priorities keep their insertion order. Comparing b to a instead of a to b inside the comparator is what turns an ascending sort into a descending one.
hints: Give the class a single private final field holding an ArrayList of Task, created where it is declared, and let add() delegate straight to that list's own add.
markDone needs an enhanced for loop that compares task.getTitle().equals(title) -- return true from inside the loop as soon as you find and mark one, and false only after the loop ends.

For pending(), first copy the not-done tasks into a new ArrayList, then call result.sort(...) with a comparator that compares the SECOND task's priority to the first, e.g. Integer.compare(b.getPriority(), a.getPriority()).
